### Abstract

Provide a 3-5 sentence summary of your work on the primary task. Indicate what input data was used, what method was used for binary class predictions, what method was used for multiclass predictions, and what estimated accuracies were achieved.

**Answer**

We developed binary and multiclass models to predict claim status from webpage text. 

For binary classification, an elastic net logistic regression model using unigram TF IDF features achieved an estimated validation accuracy of 80.2%. 

For multiclass classification, [MULTICLASS MODEL] achieved an estimated accuracy of [MULTICLASS ACCURACY]. The fitted models were used to generate binary and multiclass predictions for the 929 unlabeled test webpages.

### Preprocessing

In one paragraph lay out your preprocessing pipeline. No need to provide exact step-by-step detail; just give an overview of the main components:

-   what text content was extracted from HTML

-   how text was cleaned

-   how cleaned text was represented quantitatively

**Answer**

For binary classification, we extracted text from webpage titles, headers, and paragraphs. URLs, email addresses, punctuation, nonalphabetic tokens, short words, and common stop words were removed, and the remaining text was converted to lowercase. Terms appearing in fewer than five labeled webpages were excluded, and the remaining unigram tokens were represented using TF IDF weights learned from the training data. 

For multiclass classification, [DESCRIBE MULTICLASS TEXT EXTRACTION, CLEANING, AND FEATURE REPRESENTATION].


### Methods

Describe your final predictive models. Include one paragraph with details on the binary classification approach, and one on the multiclass approach. Include for each:

-   what ML/statistical method was used

-   model specification and hyperparameter selection

-   training method

**Answer**

For binary classification, we fitted an elastic net logistic regression model using unigram TF IDF features. The labeled webpages were divided into stratified training and validation sets. Five fold cross validation within the training data was used to select the elastic net mixing parameter and regularization strength. The selected model used an alpha value of 0.5 and was refitted using all 2,165 labeled webpages before generating the final test predictions. (OpenAI Codex was used as a coding assistant to help explain, debug, organize, and test the R code; all modeling decisions, validation results, and final outputs were reviewed by the project team.)

### Results

Indicate the predictive accuracy of the binary classifications and the multiclass classifications. Provide a table for each, and report sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy.[^1]

**Answer**

The binary classifier achieved 80.2% validation accuracy. It correctly identified 76.7% of webpages containing relevant claim content and 84.1% of webpages without relevant claim content. Its ROC AUC was 86.3%.

| Binary model metric | Estimate |
|:--|--:|
| Accuracy | 80.2% |
| Sensitivity | 76.7% |
| Specificity | 84.1% |
| ROC AUC | 86.3% |
